description: We are seeking a dedicated and experienced Licensed Nursing Home Administrator (LNHA) to lead operations at a premier health and rehabilitation center in Baltimore County, MD. This is a confidential opportunity for a visionary leader committed to delivering exceptional patient care and operational excellence.In this pivotal role, you will be responsible for the overall management of the facility, ensuring compliance with all state and federal regulations, and fostering a positive environment for both residents and staff. You will oversee daily operations, financial performance, and quality assurance initiatives, driving continuous improvement across all departments.This full-time position offers a competitive annual salary and the chance to make a significant impact on the lives of residents and the success of a reputable healthcare organization. Join a team dedicated to providing high-quality care and a supportive work environment.
requirements: Active and unrestricted Licensed Nursing Home Administrator (LNHA) license in Maryland.
Minimum of 3-5 years of experience as an LNHA in a skilled nursing or rehabilitation facility.
Comprehensive knowledge of federal, state, and local regulations governing long-term care.
Demonstrated leadership abilities with a track record of successful facility management.
Strong financial acumen and operational management skills.
salaryOrBonusInfo: Annual salary range of $115,000 - $145,000, based on experience.

description: We are seeking a dedicated and experienced MDS Coordinator (RN) to join a premier health and rehabilitation center in Missouri Valley, IA. This vital role involves ensuring accurate and timely completion of the Minimum Data Set (MDS) assessments, which are crucial for resident care planning and regulatory compliance. You will play a key part in the interdisciplinary team, contributing to the overall quality of care provided to our residents.The MDS Coordinator (RN) is responsible for coordinating the Resident Assessment Instrument (RAI) process, developing individualized care plans, and ensuring compliance with federal and state regulations. This position requires a keen eye for detail, strong clinical assessment skills, and a commitment to resident-centered care.This full-time opportunity offers an annual salary range of $65,000 - $75,000, based on experience.
requirements: Active Registered Nurse (RN) license in the state of Iowa
Minimum of 2 years of experience as an MDS Coordinator in a skilled nursing facility
Proficiency with MDS 3.0 and the Resident Assessment Instrument (RAI) process
Strong understanding of Medicare/Medicaid regulations and reimbursement
Excellent clinical assessment and documentation skills
salaryOrBonusInfo: Annual salary range of $65,000 - $75,000, based on experience.

description:
We are seeking a dedicated and detail-oriented MDS Coordinator to join a premier health and rehabilitation center in Rapid City, SD. In this vital role, you will be responsible for coordinating and completing the Minimum Data Set (MDS) assessments for residents, ensuring accuracy and compliance with federal and state regulations. Your expertise will be crucial in developing comprehensive care plans that reflect the individual needs of each resident.

This position offers an opportunity to make a significant impact on resident care by collaborating with an interdisciplinary team to ensure timely and accurate assessments. If you are passionate about quality care and have a strong understanding of the MDS process, we encourage you to apply.
requirements: Active Registered Nurse (RN) or Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) license
Prior experience as an MDS Coordinator in a long-term care setting
Thorough understanding of the Resident Assessment Instrument (RAI) process
Knowledge of Medicare/Medicaid regulations and compliance
